title: What is 'The Web' and how does it work? — Web Demystified, Ep 0

cues.text: Hello!. Welcome to Web Demystified.
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: I’m Jeremie and in this series of videos we are gonna try to make the web easy.
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: So today, in this special episode, I’m gonna give you a quick overview of what the web is and how it works.
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: Lame!
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: Yeah! Maybe there will be stuff you already know, but you could be surprised.
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: And if you’re not, show this video to someone who will be!
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: Anyway, we have to start somewhere… so let’s go!
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: Everything starts with your favorite browser where you type a web address.
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: Nope! I use Google.
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: Yes… and Google, like any other search engine that you could use, is nothing but a web site for which you have to type its web address.
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: Ok don’t worry, this is just an overview. We will talk about search engines and searching the web in another video.
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: So as you type a web address…
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: The technical name for a web address is a URL (Uniform Resource Locator)…
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: and it’s maybe better to save that for another video.
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: Overview… remember, overview.
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: So as you type a web address and hit the “Enter” key
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: OR click a link from a search page
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: your browser will send a request to the server that hosts the web site that lives at that address.
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: There, the server will process the address and it will send you back an HTML document.
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: And, yes, we will get into the details of how server and request work… in another video.
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: Next, the browser retrieves the HTML document and it reads it.
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: Usually, the HTML document contains further information telling the web browser that it needs some extra resources to render the full page.
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: For example: stylesheets (to know how to display the document)
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: images
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: or even scripts (to attach special effects).
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: Yes, you got it right… other videos to cover all of that.
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: Your browser will request all those extra ressources
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: and, once it gets all the resources, it will mix them all together to, at last, display the web page you were expecting.
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: Okay, let's recap!
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: The web is a collection of documents that will be requested by a browser from a server.
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: Each document is accessible through a web address.
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: The browser will mix all the necessary documents to turn any HTML document into a nice web page.
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: Yes, the web is nothing else than that.
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: Of course that simplicity hides many subtle things. Things that we will explore…
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: In another video!
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: Well… maybe more than one.
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: Thank you for watching our very first video.
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: As you might guess, many others are in the pipe and they should arrive very soon.
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: If you liked it, share it with your friends.
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: If you didn’t… I don't know, share it with your… arch enemy for example?
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: If you want to continue the discussion feel free to comment down below or join me and my colleagues on Twitter.
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier

cues.text: And until next time… Long live the open web! Bye!
cues.speaker: Jeremie Patonnier
